question: Must an operator have a nontrivial subspace preserved by everything commuting with it?
idea: Such a subspace is called hyperinvariant. The manuscript constructs a nonzero operator on each infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space with no nontrivial closed hyperinvariant subspace, even though its spectral radius is zero. This does not say the operator has no ordinary invariant subspaces; that is a different condition.
why: The study of collections of transformations acting on spaces of functions. These structures appear in quantum theory and infinite-dimensional geometry.

glossary.meaning: A transformation that takes a vector or function and produces another one.
A way of measuring the number of independent directions or degrees of freedom; different theories use different notions.

exactClaim: Constructs a nonzero norm-quasinilpotent operator on every infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space with no nonzero proper closed subspace invariant under every commuting operator. The construction also gives operators with no nontrivial invariant projection in the hyperfinite type II1 factor. )
